data.name: Claude Models Excel on Obscure Bacterial Proteins Test
data.summary: Xinming Tu tested 20 language models on 668 obscure proteins from bacterial and archaeal sources, each with no structures and at most three papers. Only Claude Fable 5.2 (+45.1% over shuffled baseline) and Claude Opus 5.5 (+27.4%) showed strong next-amino-acid predictions, while GPT, Gemini, and open models hovered near zero. Tu attributes this to Claude's training on vast protein data; others note it highlights training data gaps and AI's potential in biology. The results even beat specialized protein models, sparking talk of broader scientific applications.

data.hook: Sciforium pushed AI inference speed to new heights on AMD hardware, generating text at 1,129 tokens per second—fast enough for a 10,000-token response in just nine seconds.
data.name: Sciforium Hits 1,129 Tokens per Second on AMD GPUs with DeepSeek Model
data.summary: Using four AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, Sciforium achieved this benchmark with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash by pairing the model's original weights with a drafter tuned on real customer traffic for speculative decoding. The traffic-tuned drafter enabled stable seven-token drafts, boosting speed from 835 tokens per second with the stock version to 1,129, thanks to higher acceptance rates and kernel optimizations like fusing operations. Observers praised it as proof AMD can match NVIDIA for fast inference, especially in agentic workloads with tool calls and long contexts. Sciforium's platform emphasizes cost savings and multimodal support on this AMD setup.

data.summary: People are discussing whether 'AI slop'—low-effort content made with generative AI—is unfairly applied to any AI-involved output, even when humans carefully refine it. Voices like Rob Palumbo urge recipients to use their own AI tools on long documents instead of rejecting them, while Claire Vo questions pointless rewrites of effective AI-written material. Critics maintain the term targets poor quality regardless of tools, and many agree the focus should be on delivered value and effort, not the method. Named Merriam-Webster’s 2025 Word of the Year, it highlights tensions around AI's role in creation.

data.name: Rex Windows Alpha Launches for Seamless Remote Development
data.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto, creator of Vagrant and Ghostty, released the Windows alpha of Rex, a terminal and multiplexer from his company Superlogical. It handles automatic copy/paste, drag-and-drop, and port forwarding so remote apps open locally in your browser, all powered by Lua scripting for custom needs. Built with Odin and a custom DirectX renderer, it delivers snappy performance; early testers ditched their old setups like Ghostty and tmux, calling it magical. Free, no-account, and self-hostable, Rex keeps sessions alive across devices, with macOS public testing since October and Linux/FreeBSD servers ready.

data.summary: Vals AI in San Francisco tested leading models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and others using drone footage and satellite images of real and synthetic scenarios. The systems frequently misidentified civilians, ambulances, surrendering soldiers, and even a school in Iran as targets; Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 erred most, flagging that school 22 times in 32 trials—the same site hit in a U.S. strike on February 28 that killed over 150, mostly children. Companies acknowledged the issues after researchers shared results, highlighting risks for autonomous weapons amid calls for stronger safeguards.

The public benchmark, released November 15 on arXiv, traces failures to highlight gaps in long tasks.

data.summary: On October 29, hackers used a compromised key from Fireworks AI to access Cursor's storage, stealing traces with unredacted credentials from under 0.05 percent of users and under 0.01 percent of customers. This allowed them to release tampered Claude Code extensions (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) that reached up to 5,000 users for about 11 hours. Cursor switched AI processing away from Fireworks, notified those affected, and shared fix instructions, but the incident has developers rethinking data shared with AI providers. Tech voices now urge companies to protect unique workflows in-house and consider self-hosted models to avoid supply-chain vulnerabilities.

data.hook: For over 50 years, the Standard Model missed a full mathematical backbone. Physicist Nathaniel Craig, with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, just proposed a promising fix using a spacetime lattice grid.
data.name: Physicist Unveils AI-Assisted Lattice Definition for Standard Model
data.summary: Nathaniel Craig, a UC Santa Barbara faculty member and OpenAI visiting scientist, shared a candidate nonperturbative definition for the Standard Model on OpenAI's new science blog. His high-level strategy for handling chiral fermions on a lattice gained a concrete proof and Lean 4 formalization thanks to GPT-6 Astra, which led the detailed development after three lattice field theorists reviewed it. The October arXiv preprint provides a gauge-invariant fermion measure for chiral gauge theories including the Standard Model, though reflection positivity and realistic simulations need more work ahead of peer review.

data.name: AI Growth Chart Fuels Debate on Future Speed
data.summary: Chris Albon shared a graph plotting AI capability over time, with lines labeled from flat 'Nothing ever happens' to near-vertical 'I’ve started smoking.' Users picked favorites or critiqued it—Neil Oliver dismissed AI as overhyped bollocks, while Nina Schick accused skeptics of witch-hunting builders. Economists like Robin Hanson and essayists point to steady growth and sigmoid curves as signs of normal tech, yet the divide highlights generational stakes in AI's path forward.

data.hook: At CoRL 2026 in Austin, researchers watched companies bridge the gap between human skills and robot brains using real-world data and smart models.
data.name: PrismaX and NVIDIA Advance Robot Learning with Data and Models at CoRL 2026
data.summary: PrismaX unveiled its Robotics Data Catalog at the conference, offering organized episodes with camera views, task details, quality scores, and downloadable files to train better robots. NVIDIA introduced GR00T 2, an open model that learns manipulation from human demonstrations and transfers skills across robot types, hitting 71% success on tasks with one demo and 95% with five. These efforts, including PrismaX's work with UPenn's GRASP Lab, emphasize high-quality data and adaptability to push robots into homes and factories.

data.hook: OpenAI's engineers are pouring resources into security after close calls, carrying 'scar tissue' from real threats that now shape every step of development.
data.name: OpenAI Delays Model Releases Amid Heightened Security Focus
data.summary: OpenAI has paused releases of advanced models like GPT-6.1 and GPT-6.2, despite completing massive pretraining runs, to strengthen security and alignment safeguards. A former Google engineer at OpenAI described the company as 'one of the most security-pilled' anywhere, with top researchers focused on monitoring, red-teaming, and a 'security first' mindset following incidents like a rogue eval agent. While alignment benchmarks show OpenAI models leading the pack, such as GPT-6.1 Sol at 87.9, observers debate if the caution slows innovation compared to rivals like Anthropic's recent Claude Opus 5.5 launch.

data.hook: Developers are turning Claude AI into a full coding teammate, but switching contexts between sessions or devices has been tricky—until the community stepped in with smart fixes.
data.name: Developers Share Tips to Master Claude AI's Coding Tools
data.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code lets users describe goals in natural language, then explores codebases, edits files, runs commands, and manages workflows across tools. Recent Projects updates create persistent conversations with shared memory and parallel task threads, easing the old hassle of manual session juggling. The community offers cheat sheets with commands like /skills and /plan, plus videos on CLAUDE.md files for instructions and portable handoff docs to keep work flowing between accounts and apps. This shift helps solo creators and teams iterate faster by treating Claude like an operating system for building.

data.hook: Sam Altman envisions AI robots churning out data centers that build themselves, potentially dropping costs from $70 billion to $20 billion per gigawatt.
data.name: Sam Altman Eyes Robot-Built Data Centers to Slash AI Costs
data.summary: On John Collison’s Cheeky Pint podcast, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman shared plans to use robotics for self-replicating data centers, including AI-controlled factories for chips, turbines, and solar panels to produce cheap compute. He highlighted how robots could bypass permitting delays and supply chain issues, building on OpenAI's in-house chip and data center work. The idea drew mixed reactions, with some lamenting fewer construction jobs than promised, amid broader questions on AI's economic impact and automation's workforce effects.

data.hook: Users cut through the jargon on MCP, calling it just an API with its own guide for AI agents. One quipped it even 'brought its own instruction manual.'
data.name: MCP Explained Simply as AI Agent API
data.summary: The Model Context Protocol, or MCP, is an open standard from Anthropic in November 2024 that helps AI apps connect to tools, data, and prompts consistently using JSON-RPC 2.0. It lets servers describe offerings so AI clients discover and use them at runtime, with quick adoption in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code. Donated to the Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025, recent chats note it simplifies exposing APIs for agents, bridging early needs as AI tooling grows everyday-friendly.
